rationale: Third-party (TransAlta) plant supplying steam and power to Sarnia chemical hosts under long-term contracts; surplus to the IESO grid. 3 GTs + 2 condensing STs (120 MW) + back-pressure STs (56 MW): most output is grid power, so only ~30% of generation is counted as host cogeneration. The two plants it absorbed in 2000-2003 were host-owned (industries class) before that, so first_year 2003. One host (Suncor) is a refinery, not Chemical Products.

Third-party (Northland) gas combined cycle on mill land supplying mill steam; contracted 236 MW mostly grid power. Mill idled March 2017, so last_year 2016. Steam partly from auxiliary boilers (up to 350,000 lb/h), so a small host fraction.

Third-party plant with a long-term contract to supply steam and thermal services to the Chrysler/Stellantis assembly plant; power to the grid under an OEFC contract (to 2031). Smaller plant built for the host, so half the generation counted.
Third-party (Veresen, Capital Power since 2017) plant supplying electricity and steam to a local industrial host. Host identity and steam volume not confirmed in sources found; low confidence.
Third-party (Westcoast Power, later Whitby Cogeneration LP) plant at the Atlantic Packaging mill; power sold to Ontario Hydro / grid under a 20-year agreement, waste-heat steam to the mill.

Third-party (Brookfield) 110 MW combined cycle next to Algoma; contract with the province to 2014, then shut. Algoma bought it in 2018, after which it is host-owned (industries class) and already in StatCan's industrial generation, so not counted from 2018. Steam supply to Algoma before 2014 not confirmed; low confidence.

rationale: 156 MW gas plant at Cardinal attributed to Macquarie / Cardinal Power of Canada; sources link Cardinal Power to a 15 MW Ingredion cogeneration unit (2017) but do not confirm the 156 MW plant supplies Ingredion steam. Excluded until confirmed.
120 MW gas plant; no source found naming a paper mill steam host. Excluded until confirmed.

Third-party 550 MW gas cogeneration; power to Hydro-Quebec under a 20-year contract. Largely idle from 2008 (power output suspended by agreement with Hydro-Quebec) apart from steam for an industrial park neighbour, so only 2006-2007 counted, and only a small host fraction. Host sector assumed Chemical Products (Becancour park is mainly chemicals and metals).

TC Energy (ex-TransCanada) owns two LM6000 gas turbines with heat recovery steam generators inside the Irving Oil Saint John refinery; 20-year tolling deal, Irving supplies the fuel and buys all heat and electricity, so all generation is attributed to the refinery. 88-90 MW; in service Dec 2004 / 2005. Capacity factor 0.6 assumed.
